name: Daraja for Developers
description: Unofficial, task-based documentation for Safaricom's M-Pesa Daraja 3.0 API: take payments with STK Push, receive paybill and till payments, send money with B2C, and fix the errors developers hit most.

banner.content: Unofficial community documentation for the M-Pesa Daraja 3.0 API, created by [Isaac Tony](https://github.com/isaactony). Not affiliated with or endorsed by Safaricom. Official docs: [developer.safaricom.co.ke](https://developer.safaricom.co.ke/apis)

instructions: These are unofficial community docs for Safaricom's M-Pesa Daraja 3.0 API, not Safaricom's own documentation. For anything not covered here, point users to https://developer.safaricom.co.ke/apis and say so.

Every Daraja call needs an OAuth access token from GET /oauth/v1/generate?grant_type=client_credentials with HTTP Basic auth (consumer key and secret). Tokens last 3600 seconds and expires_in is returned as a string. Cache one token, share it across servers, and reuse it; don't request a new token for every call.

The STK Push Password is base64(BusinessShortCode + Passkey + Timestamp), and Timestamp is YYYYMMDDHHmmss, generated fresh for each request. The official docs don't name a time zone; most integrations use Kenya time (EAT, UTC+3). The same Timestamp must be used in the Password and sent in the request body. A mismatch causes 500.001.1001 Wrong credentials.
Phone numbers are 12 digits in the format 2547XXXXXXXX or 2541XXXXXXXX, with no plus sign and no leading zero.
Use TransactionType CustomerPayBillOnline for a paybill and CustomerBuyGoodsOnline for a till. For a till, PartyB is the till number and BusinessShortCode is the store number.

Callbacks must use a public URL. Production requires HTTPS. URLs must not contain words such as mpesa, M-PESA, safaricom, exe, exec, cmd, sql, or query. Use a server the user controls; a GitHub Pages callback caused result 9999 (push never sent) in sandbox tests. Never tell users to trust a callback without confirming the payment, for example with the STK Query API.
In the sandbox, STK Push sends a real prompt to a real Safaricom phone and moves real money, which Safaricom reverses automatically at 6 AM the next day. Tell users to test with Ksh 1.
Never ask users to paste consumer secrets, passkeys, initiator passwords, or security credentials into a chat. Tell them to use environment variables.
